title: About these notes
label: A00
summary: An explorable SQL and pandas reference, 65 Leetcode problems, SQLBolt lessons, and both SQL game walkthroughs.

title: SQL ↔ pandas translation sheet
label: A01
summary: SQL and pandas expressions are equivalent only when they return the same rows and columns, with the same treatment of missing values, duplicates, and ordering. Compare the operation’s behavior, not just its syntax.

title: Setup and conventions
label: A02
summary: Every exercise has its own tables. SQLBolt examples use its tutorial schema; the Leetcode SQL targets MySQL 8 or later. Do not combine unrelated examples into one database script.

title: SELECT queries 101
label: B01
summary: SELECT chooses the columns returned from a table. Naming columns controls the output schema; * returns every column. A projection does not remove duplicate rows.

title: Numeric constraints
label: B02
summary: WHERE filters rows before projection or aggregation. BETWEEN includes both endpoints; IN tests membership. Combine conditions with AND or OR.

title: Text constraints and LIKE
label: B03
summary: LIKE patterns use % for zero or more characters and _ for exactly one character. Equality matches a complete value. NOT LIKE excludes matching non-NULL values.

title: DISTINCT, sorting and pagination
label: B04
summary: DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows. ORDER BY controls order, DESC reverses it, and LIMIT/OFFSET choose a slice after sorting.

title: Review · Simple SELECT queries
label: B05
summary: The review combines projection, country filters, ordering and pagination using north_american_cities. It occupies the position between lessons 4 and 6; SQLBolt labels it a review rather than Lesson 5.

title: INNER JOIN
label: B06
summary: An INNER JOIN returns matching rows from both tables. Join movies.id to boxoffice.movie_id; qualify columns with aliases to make their origins clear.

title: OUTER JOINs
label: B07
summary: LEFT JOIN preserves the left table’s rows, including unmatched ones. RIGHT JOIN preserves the right side; FULL JOIN preserves both. SQLBolt’s exercise environment here uses LEFT JOIN.

title: NULL and unmatched rows
label: B08
summary: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL test missing values. An unmatched outer-join row contains NULLs on the missing side. A missing value is not automatically equivalent to zero or an empty string.

title: Expressions and aliases
label: B09
summary: Expressions calculate values in a query; AS gives the result a readable name. Arithmetic can convert units, combine sales or identify even years.

title: Aggregates and GROUP BY
label: B10
summary: Aggregates collapse rows into summary values. Without GROUP BY the entire input is one group; with GROUP BY there is one result per group. COUNT(*) counts rows, whereas COUNT(column) excludes NULL.

title: WHERE versus HAVING
label: B11
summary: WHERE filters individual rows before aggregation. HAVING filters grouped results after aggregation. Choose the clause according to whether the condition describes an input row or a group result.

title: Logical query order
label: B12
summary: The lesson’s logical order is FROM/JOIN → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT/OFFSET. This explains which values and aliases are available to each clause.

title: INSERT rows
label: B13
summary: INSERT adds rows to a table. An explicit column list makes the relationship between fields and values clear and allows omitted columns to receive defaults.

title: UPDATE rows
label: B14
summary: UPDATE changes the columns named in SET for rows matching WHERE. Omit WHERE only when changing every row is intentional.

title: DELETE rows
label: B15
summary: DELETE removes matching rows but leaves the table schema. A statement without WHERE removes all rows.

title: CREATE TABLE and schemas
label: B16
summary: CREATE TABLE declares column names, types and optional constraints. The lesson introduces primary keys, uniqueness, NOT NULL, checks, foreign keys and defaults; the exercise table itself has no constraints.

title: ALTER TABLE
label: B17
summary: ALTER TABLE changes an existing schema. The exercises add two columns, one with a default. The lesson also discusses dropping columns and renaming tables.

title: DROP TABLE
label: B18
summary: DROP TABLE removes both the rows and the table definition. IF EXISTS avoids an error when the table is already absent.

title: Additional topic · Subqueries
label: B19
summary: A subquery supplies a scalar, a list or a derived table to another query. A correlated subquery refers to the current outer row. IN and NOT IN can test membership in query results.

title: Additional topic · Set operations
label: B20
summary: UNION appends and deduplicates rows; UNION ALL preserves duplicates. INTERSECT retains shared rows. EXCEPT returns left-side rows absent on the right. Set operations require compatible corresponding columns.
